item.title: Re: The Mist Wanderer
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy, Fantasy

Elevator Pitch: A Humanoid entity from a higher universe whose misty shadow is only seen by kids.

Central Narrative: Scp XXX is a humanoid with no distinguishing features and a body seemingly made of mist. It’s height is variable, but is circa 36.5 meters or taller. that passes over our world on its travels. Scp XXX is unable to be contained due to it being impossible almost impossible to interact with. Containment has also been deemed unnecessary due to its inability to be seen by 99.98% of the population above age 13. Only kids can see it, due to the fact that they are less firmly rooted in our reality. Besides the sitings by kids, there is a slightly higher hume level around the entity. It is unknown whether there are multiple of these entities or if it is only only one that can appear in multiple places at once, as it has bee seen in multiple places at once.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Two agents, Agent Fox and Agent Hen, are tasked with tracking down the entity to take measurements around it. They are traveling with a little kid giving directions, but the kid is not very good at it. Fox is starting to lose their patience while Hen is trying to work with Fox and the kid. Hen is much better than Fox at dealing with the kid. Fox has no motherly instinct and keeps scaring the kids and just generally not knowing how to deal with them

Additional Notes: I don't know if they should be researchers or agents, but I think it works either way. The majority of the article will be audio logs of tracking the entity and interviews with kids. Fox and Hen will be the main personnel involved in the containment of scp XXX and will be in each audio log.

item.title: Re: Deletions 70: If the fact will not fit the theory – let the theory go.
item.content:encoded:
/scp-5965 (no title) by CyberKat233 deleted at -25 and three votes.

SCP 5965 is an Apple-II computer that appears brand new even tho it was discovered [REDACTED]

Feedback ported:

[+] from Nipixel_Paxel
– hide block

I see some SPaG (Spelling and Grammar) errors in the article, but I also see formatting errors.
Generally, authors will follow the guide that is linked here. You can also find this article by going onto the sidebar and clicking “How to Write an SCP.”
Anyway onto the criticism of the article itself.
The concept is interesting, however the article is a bit short and there’s no meat to it, if you get what I’m saying. Maybe flesh it out a bit, add something you find interesting about the SCP.

/scp-5188 (no title) by Duccy boi deleted at -26 and three votes.

SCP-5188 is a standard amazon box, with no anomalous effects. SCP-5188's anomalous affects only trigger when touched. When touched, SCP-5188 will suddenly sprout human arms and legs, through the bottom. It looks like a mother████ing cardboard spider. SCP-5188 will then undergo a rage state, where it will kill everything in its path by [DATA EXPUNGED] them.

Feedback ported:

[+] from DrKinyonori
– hide block

First off, I am new to this site, but I still want to give you critique.

Object Class: KETER OH GOSH RUN

Keter means hard to contain, not dangerous. Also, you should not be putting this type of emotion in your writing. Have you ever written an informative essay? Would you put 'THE CHEETAH CAN RUN SUPER FAST DANGER!' in your writing? The answer is no, and it's even more emphasized on this site.

SCP-5188's cell door must be chained by 10 heavy padlocks, have a 5 digit access code, a level 4 card reader, and voice and oral recognition. NOBODY is allowed into SCP-5188's cage UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES (See incident 5188-A-1).

This contradicts itself. You say nobody is allowed in, but it has a level 4 card reader, and an access code. If the former is the current containment procedure, you should strike-through the other part to show it's not valid anymore.

It looks like a mother████ing cardboard spider.

You're writing a research paper, and you decided to put a swear word in your formal report. You need to use plain and professional tone; this is supposed to be a research document on a dangerous object, and you need to write the part.

SCP-5188 is a standard amazon box, with no anomalous effects. SCP-5188's anomalous affects only trigger when touched. When touched, SCP-5188 will suddenly sprout human arms and legs, through the bottom.

There's no narrative to this, and it seems like 'a thing that does a dangerous thing when x happens' cliché. Is there any research into why it does this or how it magically conjures up legs and arms?

SCP-5188 will then undergo a rage state, where it will kill everything in its path by [DATA EXPUNGED] them.

But.. why? I read this and came out feeling bored, because there's no plot or anything; just a dangerous thing which does not have any form of development.

Exactly 69 seconds (1 minute and 9 seconds) after a human is killed, more "cardboard spiders" drag them away.

Wait, how are more cardboard spiders coming out? I thought there was one box which sprouted legs and arms. Also, 69? Really?

therefore they are dubbed SCP-5188-1, and are to be treated as such.

The word choice here is suboptimal. You should say something such as, '(these entities are hereinafter referred to as SCP-5188-1.)'

INCIDENT-5188-A-1:

First off, before the incident, there was a Level 4 padlock. Level 4 clearance is rarely given out to administrative personnel, and even so, why would a Level 4 administrative personnel be in close proximity to a dangerous anomaly?

Dr. ███: THE ████? Is this normal? Ill write this down.

This is not normal human dialogue. A professional researcher wouldn't say this out loud.

Dr. ███: OH ████ ITS WEARING HIS FACE AND ITS ████ING SMILING AT ME! ITS ████ING SMILING! WHAT THE F-

I thought that he would've been prepared for the inevitable, since this was already written in the document before the test (I presume.)

SCP-5188 jumps through the glass and tackles Dr. ███. It then proceeds to
[DATA EXPUNGED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

Huh? Why are there 3 redactions on 3 different lines? This makes no sense. Redactions =/= mystery value; only if they're done right. There's a good guide to redactions here.

Overall, this is a messy and rushed article, and I'm pretty sure this is a cold post as well. -1.

Forum category: Per Page Discussions / Per page discussions
Forum thread: SCP-6666-J

There's something really interesting happening here. The containment procedures and description have this perfect balance of fleshed-out detail and conciseness. It implies an article that isn't forthcoming; it sets up an expectation that despite the OOC context of the topic and despite the J in the title, this is going to be a serious piece. I think I forgot that I was reading a -J. There's nothing funny about the top half of the article, in my opinion, it is very much how I feel the Foundation would respond to this absurd scenario, and what could have been handled immaturely is handled with grace - without so much as a "(sic)" - respecting the reader enough to assume that they are reading maturely.

Then the interview happens, and it's the kick that sets off the dominoes. We know exactly what happens and there's a chain of events hidden behind the almost childish "ow!". There's a subtle but brilliant contrast between that and the article, but what gets me most is that it's all in the reader's head - the article is never explicitly funny, it never stops treating the reader like an adult. I was not expecting to find a laugh so far through such a short article.

I feel like I've seen this tried before, but never as well as it's done here. Even outside the context of the -J, the article makes sense, everything about it is justified. There's nothing here that doesn't serve a purpose, with even apparently-extraneous detail setting up the juxtaposition.

+1


Forum category: Per Page Discussions / Per page discussions
Forum thread: SCP-6666-J

-J articles are the ones that rely most on a snap judgement; the joke doesn't, or at least shouldn't, rely on several minutes of contemplation or having the gag explained to you.

At the risk of showing myself as a bit of a clod, I don't get the joke beyond "it looks like a dick + it takes your dick." It's not a funny joke so much as a motion in the direction of a joke. Maybe there's some subtle or subversive humor, but then if the joke has to be explained, it's not a good joke. -1

item.title: Re: The Bartender
item.content:encoded:
Hey! Thank you for sharing this in IRC! Here is my crit:

nitpick
hotpocket!

As a reader, I would like to know more about the "respiratory sound problems" the object suffers from. Also, what specific languages can the object speak and understand? Can it also write?

SCP-XXXX is a reality-altering entity with numerous anomalous abilities.

What are these other abilities?

All things related to the entity's origins must all be kept away from it.

3. Because it is also what is giving it mental health problems.

Mental health is a very sticky subject, my suggestion is to either get a lot of information and help from someone suffering from it, or write about your own experiences. Anyway, writing personally, the object reads like it could be suffering from Bipolar Disorder or Borderline Personality Disorder. (Bipolar feels like being silenced, but all one can do is whisper. That's the vibe I get from your SCP object.)

I have a few comments about this paragraph in general. Why is the object so passive? With such a violent back story I assume it would be more aggressive?

This wraps up my crit! I hope this helps, and again, thank you for sharing this!

Edit: I threaded the wrong post. My apologies!

item.title: SCP Hardcore RP Project | Minecraft Server

Hello fellow SCP-Enthusiasts,

I've been working on a minecraft SCP server this past month with my team, with plans to expand and all that. We're looking for some committed players, possibly some additional staff who know their stuff when it comes to RP.

The game will take place in a Site centered around an alternate version of StarPhoenix's Falling Stars cannon, where players will need to survive an event which removes the surface of life and confines all personnel to the Site with D-Class, SCPs, and limited rations. Players can be researchers, admins, security, MTF team mates, Intelligence Agents, Engineers, Medical staff, D-Class, or the single still open role of Ethics Committee Liaison. We are serious Roleplayers, so our server is whitelisted and we will be recording what Roleplay we can. We will also be making this particular map a sealed map, meaning when you die you will not be able to return to this particular iteration.

We also have bigger plans after this map, mainly our SCP: Operations project where we will conduct Foundation operations on a map with unknowing players.

To sign up now, check out our discord below and fill out a whitelist app. The beta for this map will be this Saturday, the 12th through Sunday the 13th. Full release is scheduled for December 19th if we can get enough people signed up. I'm also open to any questions (at least questions that don't require a security clearance).

item.title: SCP idea: The immortal Cow
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre : Horror, sci-fi

Idea: The idea is simply a creature with god like powers who acts like a simple cow if not disturbed.

Central Narrative: A simple cow apparently of normal size, however the animal cannot die having out of the ordinary regenerative abilities. If every single particle of the Cow were disintegrated, the beast according to some mysterious laws, would be able to move in the abdomen of a living being of its choice in the form of a fetus, and then exit the victim by ripping his intestine. If the cow were to be eaten (even just a part of its body, not all of it) it would not only do the things explained above, it would also transform consumers into half-cow men full of blood and milk. When the cow reaches two years of age, it will no longer grow and will develop the ability to teleport. If one were to drink its milk or its derivative, the subject would begin to go crazy, seeing strange demons coming out of the sky and hearing aching animal screams. The only way to capture the animal is to capture it in its fetus form and put it in a cage who resembles a hill full of grass with a light blue sky and a bright light, similiar to the sun.

Additional Notes: I think that no creature similiar to this one exist and I think it's quite a cool idea, if you are interested I can link the sandbox


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: SCP idea: The immortal Cow

Wow, that was unexpected! It's like I gave you a list of the notes I was hoping to hit, and you wrote a post saying I hit them.

+ Clearance Level -1 Instructions
- For general dissemination

While doing research for a tale series, I noticed that LurkD has a tendency to do sequential collapsibles with security clearance levels; not something I was thinking about while doing this, but you reminded me of it and yeah, I think that kind of thing is neat.

You're right about the characters, they're really just there to enable the narrative — enough of a human touch that we understand why the note at the bottom was erroneously left in, so that we understand what's going on when we see the note again in the final iteration. Hopefully enough that we get a sense of a real world about to end. I was hoping for a little poignancy, but didn't figure I'd get a lot. I'm glad there was enough there for you.

I haven't gotten around to reading Arbelict's Proposal yet, but at a glance I can see what you mean.

I liked the idea that the first few levels of clearance were nested layers of bullshit, so that everyone but O5 was getting a sanitized version of the truth. A whole spectrum of sanitization for the end of the world.

I agree that this is the kind of scenario that happens all the time, as time travel is a popular topic, but we never really think about what happens to the versions of ourselves who get offed when we set right what once went wrong. I have a time loop SCP of my own, and this one is a direct response to its implications.

For me, the reader's universe being erased while the page refreshes was the vital component of the whole thing. That moment was what I wrote everything else to support, and I'm very glad it works for you.

(I've been going through the most popular classes, using them as inspiration one by one, and the thing I hate about Apollyon [beyond the fact that it's edgelordy] is that it's universe-ending stuff by nature, and my stories are all interconnected, and I'm not looking to end that universe any time soon. This was my solution!)

Thanks for catching the Containment Class mistake! And here I thought I'd combed over every word enough times already. Nope. Fixt!

Anyway yes, I really, really appreciate this comment. Not that I don't appreciate the comments from people who wanted more and didn't get it, but it's great to know that the target audience found something effective here. Thank you very much indeed.

item.title: Forum Crit Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

item.title: Re: A Deconstruction of the Foundations Modus Operandi (SCP)
item.content:encoded:
This kinda feels like it exists in a weird place in relation to the decommissioning department (see e.g. SCP-4456-D or Mission: Decommission) where like, it kinda feels like this justifies why that department even exists whilst also not actually providing that strong a justification for it: it being dangerous to destroy an anomaly is only one reason why the Foundation doesn't do it.

Beyond this, I don't have a clear idea of the narrative: there appears to be an assumption that Miller finds out 1609 isn't real but there's not actually anything which says that happens and I'm a little unsure of what the actual core plot beats are. My concern is using the deadly virus as a backdrop for this feels…odd? In part because the disease feels very reminiscent of SCP-3862 in terms of what it actually is; but also in part because it feels like it should be a major part of the story but instead it just feels kinda like a backdrop that's there but very interchangeable?

I obviously share Grigori Karpin's concerns r.e. the antisemitism in here; though I feel like toning down the horror of that and leaving it as more of a revenge thing might work?

item.title: Re: Friendship bracelet seeking greenlight
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

This bracelet then compels its wearer to create "friendship bracelets" out of available materials and attempts to convince others to wear these bracelets

I'm not generally a fan of angles like this: it feels like it'd be a more compelling story if the person wearing it was like, 'wow not feeling negative emotions is great i have to share this', whereas if they person is forced to, their choice to spread it isn't as impactful.

The agent will have been tortured, along with their partner dying to the torture, and was recovered along with the SCP when an MTF was deployed.

W-why was the agent tortured? There feels like there's a huge narrative jump from 'we are investigating a cult' to 'the cult does horrible things' without any clear like…progression/explanation. Like, yeah okay the cult don't know it's wrong fine but that doesn't mean it's something they're naturally going to jump to doing?

My largest concern with this narrative is just…it feels very predictable? There's a generic evil cult doing bad things and the foundation swoops in and saves the day, and I'm left just…kinda wishing you did more with this? My concern is 'removes negative emotions' is…something which has been proposed a lot and so exploring it more won't necessarily be interesting; but if you can find an angle tying the foundation in to it, it'd likely work.

item.title: Re: Grant Request For Anti-Fire fire
item.content:encoded:
It's…fine? It feels too much like a sequence of events without like, a strong driving force pulling the story along or like, a big narrative hook, so my concern here is like, what is making a reader keep reading through this?

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Some pages may be mixed up with each other.

Elevator Pitch: A biomechanical structure, facility that enables the SCPF Universe to be replicated with articles and texts

Central Narrative: A Bio-Mechanical tool can completely replicate the SCPF universe. it does this with articles and pages where the articles are composed. Thanks to these pages, it can also create SCPs such as SCP-3812. Likewise, an ambiguous paradox emerges as it can replicate itself within itself. Likewise, because the SCP foundation is able to modify the articles created by this SCP (i.e., they become the administrators of the SCP-Wiki that SCPF copied), they can disrupt a sub-universe, in the same way a sub-SCPF universe can disrupt a sub-universe in this way such a paradox arises. . Well, there is a real question we have to ask. Was the SCPF universe likewise created by this Bio-Mechanical structure? And is the structure we call "Internet" actually the beginning of this paradox?

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A new SCPF universe within the SCPF universe, and so on, as well as raising awareness that these Universes are editable and the SCPF itself is a universe of fiction.

Additional Notes: I would like the reader to focus on the changes between universes and that we are the main owners of this machine.

item.title: A Quaint Little Farm Town On Top of Several Kilometers of Ice
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:
Elevator Pitch:

SCP-XXXX refers to an inhabited region consisting of a small town and outlying farmland, located inland of the Transatlantic Mountains, south of the Ross Ice Shelf. Residents of SCP-XXXX refer to it as "Shackleton County." SCP-XXXX's fields can be seen to contain plants, resembling typical crops, in tilled snow, through unknown means. Residents of SCP-XXXX do not seem to suffer from discomfort or serious harm in the their cold environment, even without specialized clothing, but appear and behave typically in all other respects. Residents have been observed to use vehicles resembling large, closed-cabin snowmobiles comparable to personal automobiles and freight trucks. Residents are observed to leave the area of the "county" only once each month, when an organized group of 50-100 residents form a convoy, identifying their destination as "Erebus City." These departures are always accompanied by a blizzard causing near-total loss of visibility for Foundation observers, and attempts to track their location by other means have always failed to date. These convoys invariably return four days after their departure, similarly obscured, carrying personal and commercial goods. It is unknown where or how these items are obtained.

Central Narrative:
Central Narrative:

Containment of SCP-XXX relies heavily on Foundation sites disguised as research bases. In particular, sites on the Ross shelf are considered to be critical to the goal of maintaining containment without alerting SCP-XXXX's residents to containment efforts. Citing fears that such sites might be rendered unusable in the future if climate change causes the ice shelf to recede, a senior researcher proposes a plan under which the Foundation would become actively involved in fighting climate change. This proposal is rejected on the grounds that climate change is an element of consensus reality, and the potential threat to SCP-XXXX's containment is distant and insufficient to justify action. Convinced of the necessity of Foundation involvement in the issue, she seeks to undermine the consensus status of climate change by spreading memetic agents through public channels. While unsuccessful in creating the circumstances for Foundation intervention, this contributes to the popularity of denial movements regarding climate change, as well as dangerous containment breaches.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The use of a classic horror setting - Antarctic mountains - for a mostly-normal settlement, and the idea of a Foundation employee trying to force the Foundation into action outside its norms

Additional Notes: Honestly, this could easily become too polemical or goofy. I think it's a good basis, though.

item.title: Re: The Monster that Didn't Exist
item.content:encoded:
Hey, thanks for the crit!

Here are my responses:
Wooooosh

1) Show at least two or three scientists getting weapons. If you really want to be fancy, show one getting to a weapons locker before getting killed, one getting a weapon before being killed, and the third shooting but missing before he's killed.

I don't… really know if this would work, purely for in-Universe reasons. This is an observation Site, nothing more, so it is unlikely that weapons are stored there. However, even if they were, these are scientists not trained for combat of any kind, so they most likely wouldn't know how to operate weapons in the first place. However (again), even if these scientists had combat training, they are up against an entity who is non-existence's hate made manifest (this monster, like the primary anomaly, doesn't exist), so the scientists would know that weapons, even anomalous ones, wouldn't work. This is why I believe this wouldn't work here. For almost any other article, this would be a great example of natural escalation, but here it just doesn't work logically.

2) The scream in his ear should increase in volume with each death. It should help your tension just a little more and add to the end.

This could work, I'll consider it. But I'll also consider that as the monster kills people, the pattern screamers would get less angry, not more, so I dunno if this would make sense.

3) Also, you need to have the "There can be only ten" come out somehow at least three ways before he gets it. Yeahyeah, I know I'm giving you lots of patterns to play with and I'm probably going over somehow. However, that's because patterns have strength, and I figure that hearing it just once just makes it a random message. Backing with a pattern makes it hard to ignore.

Again, I'll consider this. However, I was planning for Dr Vasiliev to have a conversation (admittedly, it would be mostly one-sided) with the voices (dead colleagues) in the static who explain what the rest of the pattern screamers want, before, like the rest, their voices degenerate into screaming howling and wailing. Might be contrived, but I like the idea of Dr Vasiliev's dead colleagues giving him an explanation with the last of their sanity.

Anyway, hopefully this clears some things up. Thanks for the crit!

item.title: Re: SCP idea - The Choir of Lamentation // Greenlights and feedbacks needed
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

My biggest concern with this is that it's clearly meant to be a sad scp, but it feels like that sadness is entirely being evoked by pointing at scps that already exist and going 'look how sad this is'. Like, there's nothing inherent to this file that evokes sadness beyond the references, and so I'm left feeling like this just doesn't do enough alone?

I'm really not a fan of how reliant it is on other SCPs: this feels like it needs to do more alone, but it feels like you've written yourself into a corner where you can only really convey emotions using this by referring to other SCPs, whereas it feels like focussing a lot more on personnel and the way they feel and how this SCP affects them would really help this. The effects feel like they would create a negative feedback loop, where like, the sadder the personnel get, the sadder the SCP is and in turn that makes personnel even sadder, and it feels like you could get a really strong article out of referencing a series of events indirectly where that happens and it culminates in something really bad happening.

The main problem with this is that it might feel too compulsive or too remote: you have to balance like, conveying the emotion without making it feel too much like the SCP is forcing people to be sad.

Even if you don't go with the feedback loop idea, this feels like it needs a more well crafted story to actually evoke the sadness you want to without just relying on other SCPs.
